When [the people of the city learned] that Imad al-Din wished to surrender the city,
it grieved them greatly.
And they gathered before the fortress and insulted him shamefully,
and they hung up in front of him a washbasin and a rag,
and cried out:
"O effeminate man!
Washing garments is fitting for you,
and not kingship!"
And from the balcony {or: window} he was looking down at them,
and with his own ears he heard their insults.
And on that same night of the eighteenth of the second month of this year of the Arabs,
Imad al-Din descended from the citadel of Aleppo and went outside,
and took his seat in a pavilion that had been pitched for him.
And Saladin's men took possession of the fortress and the city,
and Imad al-Din [received] those [other] places,
and went and took up his residence in Sinjar.
And Saladin had great joy in the capture of Aleppo,
more than in all the cities that he had taken.
It is said
that as he was going up the steps in front of the gate of the fortress,
he was repeating that passage of Daniel, which is written in their Quran, saying:
"The Most High God is master over the kingdom of the earth,
and gives it to whomsoever He wills,
and sets over it the lowliest of men."
(Dan.
And he turned to the nobles who were with him and said to them:
"Now I know that the kingdom is truly established!
Believe [me],
that I never envied the deceased Nur al-Din,
except for Aleppo,
nor did I lust after anything,
except for it."
And when he had gained dominion over Aleppo,
he abolished many customs duties,
and lightened the tolls,
and distributed bountiful gifts to the amount of eight hundred and fifty thousand dinars.
And in that same battle for Aleppo,
Taj al-Muluk Buri (Turi? {OCR?}), the younger brother of Saladin, was wounded,
and fell ill for several days, and died.
It is said
that when {OCR: read ܟܲܕ݂} Saladin visited him in his illness, he said to him:
"Rejoice, for behold, we have taken Aleppo,
and it is yours henceforth!"
And he answered:
"Sovereignty is fitting for the living,
and behold, I am counted with the dead.
Believe [me],
at a heavy price you have taken it,
since one like me you have lost in taking it."
For he was valiant in battle.
And Saladin and all those present wept bitterly.
And at that time, the governor of Harem
wished to sell it to the Franks,
and the guards became aware of him.
And one day, when he went out to divert himself
and came to re-enter,
